It says sensing and drawing must come from a single visibility computation, so a creature beyond sight cannot appear in one and not the other. Your headline is 'the client draws a world, and no glyph means two things' — you are changing what gets DRAWN, and this test exists to stop drawing from diverging from sensing. It is guarding exactly the seam your campaign is working on, which is the best possible reason for it to have fired.

That makes this a good red rather than an obstacle: not a number that drifted, but a design constraint catching a change that came close to breaking it. The fix is either to route your new draw path through the same shadowcast, or — if the campaign genuinely intends drawing and sensing to diverge — to say so in a decision record and rewrite the test with the argument, because silently splitting them is the thing the assertion was written to prevent.
